## G1. Calibration of the detector's probabilities (trained on the first 50, tested on the new 100; target = wrong heart rate > 5 bpm)

A calibration slope of 1 and an intercept of 0 mean the predicted risks can be read as real probabilities. Slope below 1: predictions too extreme. Calibration-in-the-large above 0: risk under-predicted on average; below 0: over-predicted.

| measure | As specified (class weights 'balanced') | Exploratory: same model without class weights |
|---|---|---|
| n | 1265 | 1265 |
| events | 86 | 86 |
| mean predicted risk | 0.462 (0.461 to 0.464) | 0.077 (0.077 to 0.078) |
| observed rate | 0.068 (0.052 to 0.088) | 0.068 (0.053 to 0.088) |
| calibration-in-the-large | -2.882 (-3.204 to -2.560) | -0.162 (-0.472 to 0.166) |
| calibration slope | 1.470 (1.243 to 1.784) | 1.344 (1.149 to 1.599) |
| calibration intercept | -3.277 (-3.934 to -2.810) | 0.476 (0.041 to 0.958) |
| Brier score | 0.212 (0.204 to 0.219) | 0.049 (0.038 to 0.063) |
| Brier of always predicting the prevalence | 0.063 (0.049 to 0.080) | 0.063 (0.050 to 0.081) |

## G2. Is the sample big enough? (Riley et al., BMJ 2020; 5 predictors, shrinkage 0.9, delta 0.05; approximate, assumes independent subjects)

Prevalence of wrong readings in the training set: 5.9% (maximum Cox-Snell R2 = 0.361).

| assumed_R2 | n_shrinkage | n_optimism | n_overall_risk | images_needed | events_needed | events_per_predictor |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| apparent Cox-Snell R2 of the unweighted fit on the first 50: 0.050 | 878 | 268 | 86 | 878 | 52 | 10.3 |
| 15% of the maximum R2 (Riley default): 0.054 | 806 | 267 | 86 | 806 | 48 | 9.5 |
| R2 = 0.05: 0.050 | 875 | 268 | 86 | 875 | 52 | 10.3 |
| R2 = 0.10: 0.100 | 425 | 261 | 86 | 425 | 26 | 5.0 |
| R2 = 0.20: 0.200 | 199 | 246 | 86 | 246 | 15 | 2.9 |

What we have:

| set | recordings | images | events | prevalence | events_per_predictor | recordings_with_an_event | top5_recordings_share_of_events |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| first 50 (training) | 49 | 1509 | 89 | 5.9% | 17.8 | 27 | 70% |
| new 100 (test) | 99 | 1265 | 86 | 6.8% |  | 54 | 27% |

- Collins: testing a finished model needs at least 100 events. The new 100 hold 86. At 6.8% prevalence about 1,471 images would be needed (we have 1,265).
- Images are 13 to 31 versions of the same recording, so the number of independent subjects is closer to the number of recordings, and a few recordings carry many events (last column above). By this standard the detector is below the recommended sample size; read its numbers as a prototype result.

Status counts: Met 22, Partly 12, Not applicable 6, To do 3, Not met 1. Items 37 to 44 were taken from a summary of the paper, not from the checklist table: check wording against the official table (Radiol Artif Intell 2024;6(4):e240300, appendix) before quoting. 'To do' = depends on writing the report or papers.
